respStmt.resp: ratified — keyed, or confirmed against the page, by a human editor
respStmt.name: human editor

respStmt.resp: adopted — transcluded whole out of adjudicated ground truth, where a human settled every mark at the raster. No model chose these characters, so the reading is not a proposal; but no human read this document either, so it is not editorial work on the transcription. The responsible act happened one artifact upstream, and this records where. Verified on every run against the ground truth it came from, so it fails rather than going stale if that is later corrected.
respStmt.name: human editor, at the raster

respStmt.resp: proposed — read off the page image by a language model. Carries no authority over glyph identity; a reading awaiting ratification.
respStmt.name: language model, collation pass

respStmt.resp: unexamined — handwritten-text-recognition output nobody has looked at
respStmt.name: recognizer

series.title: Memoir of the American Museum of Natural History
series.note: The title page (scan 1-005) sets "Memoir of the American Museum of Natural History / New York" above "Volume VII", with no Memoirs volume number anywhere on it. "Volume XI" is read off the archival cover sheets of parts 2 and 3 (scans 2-001, 3-001), which reproduce the Memoirs series title page — a degraded photocopy, so a weak witness on its own. The AMNH catalogue record independently gives both statements ("Memoirs of the AMNH; v. 11; Publications of the Jesup North Pacific Expedition; v. 7"), which is why both are here rather than only the one the title page carries.

bibl.title: Material culture
bibl.note: No archival sheet and no part title page in the surrogate; the volume front matter stands in its place. Single-witness: the catalogue record alone, with nothing in the scans to corroborate it.

bibl.title: Religion
bibl.note: Typescript on the archival sheet (scan 2-001) reads "Part II. — The Chuckchee - Religion by W. Bogoras 1907"; the printed imprint on the same sheet reads 1904. The catalogue agrees with the typescript, so the 1904 on that sheet is the volume's date carried by the reused title page and not this part's.

bibl.title: Social organization
bibl.note: Typescript on the archival sheet (scan 3-001) reads "Part III. — The Chuckchee - Social Organization by W. Bogoras 1909"; the printed imprint on the same sheet reads 1904. Same two-witness agreement as part II.

bibl.title: The Chukchee. Memoirs of the AMNH; v. 11; Publications of the Jesup North Pacific Expedition; v. 7.
bibl.author: Bogoras, Waldemar, 1865-1936.
bibl.publisher: Leiden, E.J. Brill ltd.; New York, G.E. Stechert
bibl.extent: 3 v.: illus., 35 pl., fold. map. 36 cm.
bibl.note: One catalogue record, three PDF bitstreams — the parts are not separately catalogued, which is why part designations have to come from this record's description note rather than from a per-part entry.

The record corroborates two apparatus stores independently of the pages they were read from: "Authorities quoted": p. 3-9 against data/authorities.json's folios 3-9, and "35 pl." against data/loi.json's plates I-XXXV. Neither was consulted when those files were built.

832 pages. Each PDF carries a bitonal JBIG2 text master at approximately 300 dpi; figure photographs are separate embedded JPEGs at 150 dpi and gain nothing from re-rendering. Rasters in scans/ are exactly `pdftoppm -r 300` over these files and are derived, not source.
The record carries no rights statement, so it settles nothing about this edition's licence. The 1904 date on it is the volume's, not any part's.

projectDesc.p: A proof of concept for an open ethnographic-atlas effort: web and epub editions of public-domain ethnographies with annotated entities, indices for toponyms, species and transcribed forms, and linkage to D-PLACE.

The failure mode this edition is organised against is fluent nonsense — plausible output carrying no error signal. Hence mechanical, auditable rules over judgement; "unresolved" in preference to a confident guess; and two independent witnesses to one confident one wherever a second is cheap.

normalization.p: Unicode Normalization Form D (NFD), corpus-wide. Never NFKC: it has compatibility decompositions for two inventory glyphs and destroys them (U+1D4B to U+025B; U+02D9 to space plus combining dot).
Runs of two or more spaces are collapsed, and space before a semicolon, colon or comma is stripped. Neither is a judgement call; both are enforced rather than reported.

correction.p: Misspellings and orthographic errors in English, Russian and other European languages are corrected silently, and hyphenated words broken across lines are joined. Pre-1918 Russian orthography is not a misspelling and is not touched, nor are the source's own errors, which are recorded as printed and adjudicated in a note.

Forms in Chukchi, Koryak and Yupik are never corrected, normalized or emended. They are keyed character by character from the page, every mark read and accounted for; where the letterform does not decide, unclear says so. Hyphens are load-bearing in Americanist notation and are not joined.

interpretation.p: The character inventory, the mark-base licensing rules and the lookalike register are specified in keying_spec.md. The per-element output contract for the collation pass is in .claude/skills/transcribe-page/SKILL.md. The evidence behind the inventory — aligned pairs, flag register, per-glyph attestation — is in concordance.md.

application.label: kraken
application.desc: Layout segmentation and text recognition. Produces ALTO in gt/ and ocr/; all such output is rank #htr until a human reaches it.

application.label: CATMuS print
application.desc: Recognition model, stock and unmodified — upstream ships no version number, and version is required here and must be a version number, so the identifying witness is the sha256 each ALTO records in its Processing block rather than this attribute. Measured against human-collated text it reads approximately 91% of ASCII and 0% of the Americanist inventory, so it is a witness to line geometry and to English and to nothing else.

application.label: harness
application.desc: The project toolchain. `harness tei validate` is the gate on page files; `harness corpus normalize` is the gate on encoding.
